sections.sectionSummaryBrief: This section explains that the concept of taking the stones of the place also applies within man himself, where the letters (the inanimate aspect of his powers) draw down a very lofty light because their source is higher, similar to how the "utterance of the mouth of Hashem" in bread is higher than that in man.

translations.translation: A)
Now, the concept of "And he took from the stones of the place" etc. also exists within man himself.
And the explanation is,
for it is known82
that stones are letters83,
for just as stones are inanimate, so too are the letters the aspect of the inanimate within man's powers.
But nevertheless,
and for this very reason,
they draw down
(letters, from the term "ata"84
"boker"85,
a concept of drawing down)
an aspect of a most exalted light.
And analogous to what is known86
in the explanation of the verse87
"For not by bread alone does man live, but by every utterance of the mouth of Hashem does man live,"
that the fact that bread sustains man is because the utterance of the mouth of Hashem within the bread
(the vegetative)
is more exalted
(in its source)
than the utterance of the mouth of Hashem within man,
for this very fact that it descended lower indicates that in its source it is more exalted,
for whatever is higher descends lower,
so too is it regarding the matter of letters,
the inanimate
(within man),
for their source is higher even than the aspect of the vegetative88,
for whatever is higher
descends lower and lower.
And this is the concept of "And he took from the stones of the place and placed them at his headrest"
(as it is in the service of each and every Jew),
that the service of the aspect of letters,
the inanimate within man,
reaches higher than the service of the aspect of intellect
("at his headrest").

sections.sectionSummaryBrief: This section explains that the two interpretations of "taking the stones of the place" (service of the inanimate within man and service of refining physical things) are connected, because refining the physical world is accomplished through the inanimate power of action within man, and this reveals the essence of the soul united with His Essence.

translations.translation: B)
And the two aforementioned explanations of "And he took from the stones of the place" etc.
[the service of the aspect of the inanimate within man
(above, section 11)
and the service of refining physical things of the world
(above, section 9)]
are related to each other.
For the refinement of the matters of this physical world
(the stones of the place of the world)
is through the inanimate within man,
the power of speech,
and primarily – the power of action90,
for action is the main thing91.
And one should add,
that the connection of these two matters is not only from the aspect of the "lower" element
(stone,
inanimate)
within them
[that the action in the physicality of the world is through the lower powers within man],
but rather,
also regarding the matter of the elevation within them
("and placed them at his headrest").
That is,
that it is within the power of each and every Jew to make from his portion in the world a dwelling place for Him, blessed be He,
for His very Essence92,
is because through his service with his lower powers, the essence of the soul, which is united with His Essence, blessed be He, is revealed93.

sections.sectionSummaryBrief: This section explains that the service of the inanimate within man, which reaches above the "head" of Yaakov (the aspect of Chayah), reveals the aspect of Yechidah within him, which is the essential self-sacrifice that every Jew possesses, as it is beyond any opposition.

translations.translation: And this will be understood by prefacing what is explained in many places94
regarding the matter of the yud of the Name Havayah in the soul of man, which is the aspect of Chayah.
And since the aspect of the head of Yaakov
[which is the yud of Yaakov,
which is the yud of the Name Havayah
(as above, section 4)]
is the aspect of Chayah,
it is understood from this,
that this that the service of the aspect of the inanimate within man reaches above the aspect of the head of Yaakov
(as above
(at the end of section 11)
in the explanation of "And he took from the stones of the place and placed them at his headrest"),
the intention in this is – that through the service of the aspect of the inanimate within man,
the aspect of Yechidah within him is revealed
(which is above the aspect of Chayah).
For the concept of the service of the aspect of the inanimate within man,
is that even though he has no vitality
(neither from the feeling of the emotions of the heart,
nor from the intellect of the mind,
and also not from the will which is above intellect
(the aspect of Chayah))
nevertheless he performs his service,
this is from his essence,
that each Jew, in his essential being, wants to do everything that is the will of Hashem,
as per the well-known ruling of the Rambam95.
And this is that each and every Jew,
even the most light among the light,
can sacrifice his life for the sanctification of the Name96,
for the power of self-sacrifice is from his essence, the aspect of Yechidah97,
for regarding this level, no opposition applies,
"the reflection of a reflection has no hold on them"98.
[And this is also what the Torah promised, that ultimately Israel will do repentance etc. and immediately they will be redeemed99,
that the intention of "ultimately Israel will do repentance" is
(also)
for each and every Jew100
– for upon the aspect of Yechidah within each Jew, no opposition applies, G-d forbid, but it is in concealment,
and the Torah of Truth promises that ultimately it will be revealed].
And the Torah of truth promises that ultimately it will be revealed.
